entries.appliesTo: nonhuman entities, including agents powered by artificial intelligence, in nursing, medicine, and physician-assistant practice

sources.aiRule: § 1920(h), Title 24 — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be licensed in any of the following: (1) The practice of professional nursing.'; § 1720(k) — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be certified to practice medicine in the State.'; § 1773(d) — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be licensed as a physician assistant in the State.'
sources.profession: § 1920(h)(1)-(3) — 'The practice of professional nursing. … Practice as an advanced practice registered nurse. … The practice of practical nursing.'; § 1720(k) — 'may not be certified to practice medicine in the State'; § 1773(d) — 'may not be licensed as a physician assistant'

flags: title-use prohibition fits no listed duty: § 1920(i) — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not use any of the following titles or abbreviations' (Nurse, RN, APRN, CRNA, CNS, CNP, CNM, LPN, Doctor/'Dr.'); parallel title bans in § 1720(l) (Doctor, Physician, MD, DO) and § 1773(d) ('may not use the title physician assistant or the abbreviation "PA"')
no penalty or enforcement provision in this text; exposure omitted (silence is silence)
text on file is the Introduced/Draft version only; LegiScan status is Passed (2026-04-23) — enacted text not verified against this draft

category note: prohibition binds 'a nonhuman entity' directly (licensure ban + title ban) rather than imposing an affirmative program on a business; coded company as it constrains private AI products, not government or schools
